description: A single-expression arm body whose line ends in `+` continues onto the next line (§7.2.2 rule 2): `.Boom(m) :> "a:" +⏎ m` is one arm. (impl#1-legacy dialect — see rationale.)
rationale: IMPL#1-LEGACY behaviour (S469, dpa-073 F5): this case pins impl#1's newline-terminated reading (an arm body continues past a line break only after a continuation token such as `+`), which impl#1 keeps as a carried divergence. Under SPEC §7.2.2 as rewritten S469 (dpa-073 F1 (a)) a line break is whitespace everywhere, so the arm continues regardless, and arms are a comma list; this source (no arm commas) is not ruled-dialect input. Pre-S469 rationale, kept for the record: §7.2.2 (S446) "Arm heads" — a single-expression arm body ended at its line break unless the line ended in a rule-2 continuation token (the bootstrap once split this arm — dpa-068 D12).
